summary: Iter 86 — Validated Waivers pre-check UX and 76 router unit tests on Dynasty Dreams. All 76 router tests pass (3.39s). New live integration suite (4/4 pass) exercises happy-path precheck, requires_drop blocker (roster_size=13 + cap_enabled, with deterministic restore), claim placement + my_claims propagation, and admin regression for /leagues, /teams, /players, /trade-block, /activity. Frontend E2E: chriszarek can open the claim modal on /waivers, precheck-panel renders the 13/23 roster pill + Room badge, sonner toast 'Claim placed on Connor McDavid for $2' fires on success, and a high bid disables the confirm button and surfaces the insufficient_faab issue text correctly. League roster_size restored to 23, salary_cap_enabled=false, test waiver_claim cleaned up.

minor.issue: Legacy test_trade_waiver_engine.py::TestWaiverClaimsList::test_get_my_claims fails because it relies on a claim made by a skipped/prior fixture step — unrelated to iter 86 changes; precheck + claim verified independently in iter86 live suite.

critical_code_review_comments: Waivers.tsx file has @ts-nocheck — fine for now but the precheck typing should be hardened next iteration (e.g., a Precheck interface) to prevent runtime null-deref on precheck.cap if backend ever omits it.
Precheck addition calculation (salary synthesis) is duplicated between waivers.py precheck and roster cap calc — extract into a shared util to keep them in lockstep.

GET /api/waivers/claims returns a bare list when my_claims=true but the frontend already handles both .claims and bare array shapes — consider standardizing the envelope to {claims:[...]} across all waivers list endpoints.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (modal, precheck, toast, blocker, cancel all green)

rca of the issue: No bugs detected in iter86 scope. Pre-check, claim placement, toast, and 76 router unit tests all pass end-to-end. Single unrelated legacy test_trade_waiver_engine::test_get_my_claims failure is a fixture-ordering issue in the legacy test file (not iter86 code).
